lines.x: Inflation in the Philippines reached 7.8% in October, the highest level in 44 months, driven by soaring petrol prices linked to Middle East conflict and a devalued peso.
The Philippine peso staged a strong recovery, gaining more than half a peso against the US dollar to return to the P62 level as improved global market sentiment lifted the currency.
Philippine bank lending growth accelerated to 11.4% in September, reaching a four-month high as credit demand from businesses and consumers remained resilient, according to central bank data.
The Philippine economy grew slightly faster than initially reported in the second quarter, with GDP revised upward to 2.4% ahead of the upcoming third-quarter print.
